title: Choose Bookshelf's visual world
question: The roll assigned Photos Library. Keep it, take the pick or an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Photos Library
options.lineage: iOS Photos and Apple Music library grids
options.thesis: Her books as an iPhone library: covers edge to edge, the phone's own grammar around them.
options.viewport: Large collapsing title over a gapless three-across cover grid; a floating glass tab bar with a raised scan button under the thumb.
options.risk: Sits closest to what Apple ships; it only earns its place if the grid, sheets and gestures feel truly native.

raised.raise: State is a mark on the cover, not a colour: a stamp for read, a folded corner flag for read next.
One system face carries every size from large title to caption; no second family.
One strict grid rules the screen; covers never sit inside cards.

options.label: Card Catalogue
options.lineage: library card catalogues and date-due slips
options.thesis: Every book gets a catalogue card; finishing one stamps the date-due slip.
options.viewport: A drawer of cover-topped index cards with a brass-pull scan button at the bottom edge.
options.risk: Paper and stamps are where book apps usually land; it can slide into cream-and-serif nostalgia.

options.label: Cutting Bench
options.thesis: Covers strung as frames along a perforated rail, a tape flag where she stopped.
options.viewport: An orange field crossed by a scrubbing strip of cover frames.
options.case: Fuses cleanly as a strip of covers, but readers do not know an editing bench and a single rail hides her collection.
options.risk: Reads as a film tool, not a library.
options.kept: State as a mark, not a hue.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.thesis: Book titles set as coarse pixel type at poster scale.
options.viewport: A giant pixel title over dense justified columns.
options.case: Type would compete with the covers she wants to browse.
options.risk: The covers stop being the heart of the screen.

options.label: Centre-Rail Edition
options.thesis: Her books as two columns of small roman around a vermilion key rail.
options.viewport: Two dense text columns with a centre rail of keys.
options.case: Text-first reading layout buries covers and slows adding books.
options.risk: Scholarly and slow on a phone in a store aisle.

options.label: ASCII Render
options.thesis: Covers re-rendered as glyph density on a phosphor grid.
options.viewport: A live glyph grid standing in for cover art.
options.case: Destroys the real covers, her one brand commitment.
options.kept: One strict grid for the whole screen.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.thesis: Lists gathered and released like cloth on a cord.
options.viewport: A black semicircle that pleats into sections.
options.case: No link to books, reading or a phone in a bookstore.
options.kept: A single pull as the one primary control.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.thesis: Lists held in tension as a breathing force diagram.
options.viewport: A column of struts with books pinned to nodes.
options.case: Engineering diagram fights a personal library.
options.risk: Cold and abstract for her shelf.
options.kept: Distinct slack, balanced and stressed states.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A Goodreads or StoryGraph style reading tracker, executed well.
canonCard.viewport: Currently reading at top, shelves as rows, status buttons under each book.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the apps she could already download.
